$comment: Issue #23, FR-075. The closed refusal register. Narrowing it to make an input pass is forbidden (FR-075-CON-1); widening it is a specification amendment. The five schema keys are the measured executable surface of the pinned 0.76.0 — `JsonSchemaObject` binds `customTypePath` and `customBasePath`, the parser reads `x-python-import` and `x-python-type` as Python symbols to emit, and `default_factory` is the vector GHSA-386q-5hp3-95m9 names. FR-043's three-key set is a subset, which a gate asserts.

schemaKeys.why: the generator emits `from <module> import <name>` from this key; the vector of GHSA-5578-w22f-pfx9
the parser reads this as a serialized Python type expression and emits it verbatim
bound by `JsonSchemaObject` as a dotted Python path the generator imports; the vector of GHSA-5578-w22f-pfx9
bound beside `customTypePath` and reaching the same import machinery
the generator emits this as a callable in the generated default; the vector of GHSA-386q-5hp3-95m9

referenceShapes.why: a `$ref` carrying any URI scheme makes the generator a fetcher of caller-chosen content
an absolute filesystem `$ref` reads outside the prepared input set
a `..` segment escapes the prepared input set
a Windows drive-letter `$ref` is an absolute path in another spelling

argumentTokens.why: an option in the FR-073-CON-2 prohibited set places caller-controlled Python in the output or loads caller-controlled code
a remote-reference or lock option re-enables the fetching the profile disables
an option token absent from the allow-list is refused until it is reviewed; an allow-list that defaults to admit is not an allow-list
